# Design: Release notes in proposals and a generated changelog

## Context

- The proposal is free Markdown today: nothing in `codev-core` parses it.
  Validation (`codev-engine/src/validate/mod.rs`, `validate_change`) reads
  `change.yaml` (`metadata_rules.rs`) and the deltas, never `proposal.md`.
- The proposal instruction and template live in
  `assets/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml` and
  `assets/schemas/spec-driven/templates/proposal.md`; they have no release
  note section.
- Archived changes sit in `_codev/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<name>/`
  (spec `spec-merge`, "Sync leaves the change active; archive moves it");
  34 are archived, none with a release note. The repository has no tag yet.
- Git is already run through the `ProcessRunner` port
  (`crates/codev-engine/src/ports.rs`), e.g. `sources/update.rs` checks
  `git --version` before `git ls-remote`; `MockProcessRunner` scripts its
  responses in tests.
- `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog; `.github/workflows/release.yml`
  uses `generate_release_notes: true`.
- Contradiction observed, not settled here: the `codev` 0.6.1 binary
  installed in this environment already serves a `## Release note` section
  in the proposal instruction and has a `codev changelog` command, while this
  repository's source has neither — and that binary's proposal instruction
  does not start with `Role: product owner`, which the main `skills` spec
  requires. The plan is written against this repository's source and specs.

Constraining decisions: [0001](../../decisions/0001-functional-core-imperative-shell.md)
(the core decides, the shell executes),
[0002](../../decisions/0002-crate-graph-as-dependency-rule.md) (effects only
through the four ports, layering by crate graph),
[0003](../../decisions/0003-codev-planning-root.md) (paths resolved from the
planning root).

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals**

- One parser of the release-note format, shared by validation and by
  `codev changelog`, so the two can never disagree on what is valid.
- A pure changelog assembly (selection by set difference, grouping,
  ordering, fallback, rendering) testable without git or disk.
- Git access confined to a thin engine module behind `ProcessRunner`.

**Non-Goals**

- Writing into `CHANGELOG.md` (`--write`) or editing the release workflow to
  use the command; both can follow once the output has been used for a
  release.
- Back-filling release notes into archived proposals: archived changes are
  history, the fallback covers them.
- Scopes, links to PRs, authors or any field beyond category and text.

## Decisions

### Decision: A pure proposal-section parser in `codev-core::parser`

New module `codev-core/src/parser/proposal.rs`:

- `parse_release_note(source: &str) -> Parsed<ReleaseNote>`, with
  `ReleaseNote::{Missing, None, Items(Vec<ReleaseItem>)}` and
  `ReleaseItem { category: Category, text: String, breaking: bool, line }`;
  `Category` is a closed enum in Keep a Changelog order (its `Ord` gives the
  output order).
- `what_changes_bullets(source: &str) -> Vec<String>` for the fallback.

It reuses `parser::shared::section_header` (level-2 headings only) and the
fence handling of `parser::fence`, so a `## Release note` inside a code block
is not a section. HTML comments are stripped before reading lines, so the
template's comment does not count as content. A bullet continues on lines
indented by at least two spaces; continuation lines are joined with a space.
`breaking` is true when the text starts with `**BREAKING**`. The findings
use the codes `release_note_invalid_category`, `release_note_malformed`,
`release_note_empty`, `release_note_none_with_items` (errors) and
`release_note_missing` (warning), frozen in `codev-core::validate::codes`.

**Alternatives considered**:

- A field in `change.yaml` (`release_note: [...]`): structured for free, but
  the note would live away from the prose the product owner writes and
  reviews, and YAML multi-line text is error-prone to hand-write.
- A pulldown-cmark dependency: unjustified for one section; the project
  already parses specs line by line with the same primitives.

### Decision: Validation reads `proposal.md` only when it exists

`validate_change` gains one step after `check_change_metadata`: if
`proposal.md` exists, parse its release note and push the findings, located
at `proposal.md` with their line (`Missing` is reported at line 1). No
proposal, no finding — a change fresh from `codev new change` stays clean.
The rule is not tied to the schema name: a custom schema whose proposal has
no `## Release note` gets only the warning, which `--strict` users can
silence by adding `None`.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Gate the rule on the `spec-driven` schema: hides the feature from custom
  schemas that adopt the section, and makes the rule depend on a name
  rather than on the content.
- Missing section as an error: would fail every active change written before
  this one and block their archive (`validation_failed`); the warning plus
  `--strict` in CI gives the same pressure without breaking in-flight work.

### Decision: Range = set difference of archive folders between two trees

`codev changelog` lists the archive folder names at `--since` and at
`--until`, and keeps those only in `--until`. Membership by tree, not by the
date prefix of the folder, is what makes "between two tags" exact: a change
archived the day a tag is cut belongs to the release whose tree contains
it. The pure core function takes
`(since: BTreeSet<String>, until: Vec<(folder, proposal_source)>)` and
returns a `Changelog { sections: BTreeMap<Category, Vec<Entry>>, warnings }`;
entries sort by (`breaking` first, folder name, position in the proposal).
Folder names start with `YYYY-MM-DD-`, so lexical order is archive order.
`render_markdown(&Changelog, heading: Option<Heading>) -> String` produces
the Keep a Changelog text.

**Alternatives considered**:

- Filter by the folder's date against the tag's commit date: wrong around a
  tag cut and across time zones.
- `git log` on the archive path between the refs: misses uncommitted
  archives for the working-tree default, and is confused by merges.

### Decision: A thin git reader in `codev-engine::changelog`

New module `codev-engine/src/changelog.rs`, the only place that runs git
for this feature, through `ProcessRunner`:

1. `git --version` fails → `git_unavailable` (same as `sources/update.rs`);
   `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails → `not_a_git_repository`. The
   archive's path relative to the toplevel is derived from the `Layout`
   (decision 0003), with `/` separators for git paths.
2. Resolve each ref: a value starting with `-` is refused as `unknown_ref`
   before any call; otherwise
   `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}`, failure → `unknown_ref`.
   Only the resolved commit id is passed to later commands, so user input
   reaches git once, in a position where it cannot be an option.
3. Default `--since`: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 <until-commit>`
   (`HEAD` for the working tree); "no names found" → empty set (every
   archived change). `HEAD` itself missing (no commit yet) → empty set too.
4. List: `git ls-tree --name-only <commit> -- <archive>/`; read:
   `git show <commit>:<archive>/<folder>/proposal.md`. For the working tree,
   the `FileSystem` port is used instead (`list_dir`, `read_to_string`).
5. Heading: `--until` is a tag when `git rev-parse --verify --quiet
   refs/tags/<until>` succeeds; its date is
   `git log -1 --format=%cd --date=short <commit>`; the version is the tag
   name without a leading `v`.

Proposals are read only for folders in the difference, so the cost is one
`git show` per released change.

**Alternatives considered**:

- `gix`/`git2` crate: a heavy new dependency for five read commands, and the
  project already shells out to git behind a port.

### Decision: CLI and JSON contract

`codev changelog [--since <REF>] [--until <REF>] [--no-heading] [--json]` in
`codev-cli`. Human mode prints the Markdown on stdout and warnings on
stderr, so `codev changelog > notes.md` yields clean notes. `--json` prints
a `ChangelogReportV1` defined in `contract::v1` (not derived from the core
types): `since`, `until` (`{ ref, commit }`, `until.ref` = `"WORKTREE"` when
defaulted), `heading`, `changes: [name]`, `sections: [{ category, items:
[{ text, breaking, change }] }]`, `warnings: [{ code, change, line? }]`,
`status: []`. Exit codes: 0 on success (warnings included), 1 on an
execution error. Shell completions pick the subcommand up from clap.
`ValidateReportV1` is unchanged in shape; it only carries the new codes.

**Alternatives considered**:

- `--format keep-a-changelog|markdown|json`: `--json` is the convention of
  every other command; `--no-heading` covers the release-body case.

### Decision: Schema text

The proposal instruction gains the `## Release note` bullet in its section
list and a product owner criterion ("the release note is written for end
users, categorized, with breaking items marked, or `None` for an internal
change"); the template gains the section after `## Impact` with an HTML
comment giving the form. The installed skills are not regenerated by this
change beyond what `codev update` already does: the skills read the
instruction at run time.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The fallback publishes What Changes bullets, written for developers] →
  they go under `Changed` with a `release_note_missing` warning per change,
  so the maintainer sees what to rewrite; only the first release after this
  change is concerned.
- [A ref such as `--output=x` reaching git as an option] → refused before
  any call, and only resolved commit ids are passed afterwards.
- [Git versions lacking a flag] → only long-standing flags are used
  (`rev-parse --verify`, `describe --tags`, `ls-tree --name-only`, `show`,
  `log --date=short`); no `--end-of-options`, no `%cs`.
- [Windows paths] → git paths are built with `/` from the layout, never
  with `Path::join`; tests run on the in-memory ports with fixed separators.
- [A malformed note in an archived change] → impossible after this change
  (archive refuses validation errors), so it is only reported as a warning
  and skipped, never fatal.

## Migration Plan

- Active changes without the section: a warning; adding the section (or
  `None`) clears it. CI using `codev validate --strict` will flag them, which
  is the intended nudge.
- Archived changes: untouched; the fallback applies.
- Rollback: removing the command and the rule leaves proposals with an
  extra section, harmless Markdown.

# Proposal: Release notes in proposals and a generated changelog

## Why

`CHANGELOG.md` and the GitHub Release notes are written by hand, while every
archived change already states what it brings in its proposal: the same
information is written twice, and the hand-written copy drifts or is
forgotten. Each proposal should carry a short, categorized release note that
validation checks, so the changelog between two tags can be generated from
the archive instead.

## What Changes

- The `spec-driven` proposal gains a `## Release note` section: one bullet
  per item, `- <Category>: <text>`, with Category among the Keep a Changelog
  categories (`Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`,
  `Security`); a breaking item starts its text with `**BREAKING**`; a change
  users will not notice writes the single line `None`. The proposal
  template and the product owner's "Done when" criteria include it.
- `codev validate` checks the release note of every active change whose
  proposal exists: an unknown category, a bullet that does not follow the
  `- <Category>: <text>` form, an empty item, or `None` mixed with items is an
  error; a proposal without the section is a warning, so changes already in
  flight are not blocked (`--strict` turns it into a failing exit code).
- New command `codev changelog [--since <ref>] [--until <ref>] [--no-heading]
  [--json]`: it collects the release notes of the changes archived between two
  git refs — present in the archive at `--until` and absent at `--since` —
  and prints them grouped by category in Keep a Changelog order, breaking
  items first within a category. `--since` defaults to the most recent tag
  reachable from `--until`, or to the beginning of history when there is no
  tag; `--until` defaults to the working tree, so notes can be generated
  before the release is tagged. The heading is `## [<version>] - <date>` when
  `--until` is a tag, `## [Unreleased]` otherwise; `--no-heading` omits it,
  for a GitHub Release body.
- An archived change without a `## Release note` section (every change
  archived before this one) falls back on its What Changes bullets, listed
  under `Changed`, with a warning naming the change; a `None` release note is
  left out of the output.
- The command only reads: it writes nothing to `CHANGELOG.md`; the maintainer
  pastes or redirects its output.

Assumptions made without asking (evaluation run, no user available):

- The categories are those of Keep a Changelog, which the project's
  `CHANGELOG.md` already follows.
- A missing section is a warning, not an error, so that active changes
  written before this one still validate; malformed content is an error,
  so it blocks archive like any other validation error.
- The range is defined by the archive's content at each git ref, not by the
  archive folder dates, so a change archived on the day of a tag lands in the
  right release.
- No `--write` into `CHANGELOG.md` in this change: generation to stdout
  covers the need and keeps the command read-only.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `changelog` — the `codev changelog` command: range selection, grouping,
  fallback for archived changes without release note, output formats and
  errors.

### Modified Capabilities

- `validation` — release-note rules on a change's proposal.
- `skills` — the default schema's proposal instruction and template ask for
  the release note, and the product owner's criteria check it.

### Removed Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- `assets/schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml` (proposal instruction) and
  `assets/schemas/spec-driven/templates/proposal.md`.
- `codev-core`: a pure parser for the `## Release note` section of a proposal
  and the changelog rendering; new validation codes.
- `codev-engine`: release-note rule in change validation; changelog
  assembly reading archived proposals at a git ref through the existing
  `ProcessRunner` port.
- `codev-cli`: the `changelog` subcommand, its human and JSON output in
  `contract::v1` (new `ChangelogReportV1`; additive codes in
  `ValidateReportV1`), shell completions.
- Documentation, in `docs/en` and `docs/fr`: `reference/cli.md`
  (`codev changelog`), `reference/file-formats.md` (the `## Release note`
  section), `reference/json-output.md` (changelog report, new validation
  codes), `workflow.md` (releasing from the archive); `CONTRIBUTING.md` and
  `CONTRIBUTING.fr.md` if they describe the release routine; `CHANGELOG.md`.
- No change to `change.yaml`, to the archive layout, or to existing JSON
  fields. Changes using a custom schema are validated by the same rule only
  if their proposal contains a `## Release note` section.

## Domains

- [x] security — `--since`/`--until` are user input passed to git; a value starting with `-` must not be read as an option
- [ ] personal-data — no personal data read or produced
- [ ] user-interface — CLI output only, no interface
- [ ] performance — reads a few dozen proposals at two refs; no hot path
- [ ] operations — no logs, metrics or long-running process
- [x] migration — active and archived changes predate the section; they must keep validating and producing notes

## Release note

- Added: Each proposal of the default schema has a `## Release note` section
  — categorized bullets such as `- Added: …`, or `None` — and
  `codev validate` checks its form.
- Added: `codev changelog` generates the release notes of the changes
  archived between two git refs (by default, since the last tag), grouped by
  Keep a Changelog category, as Markdown or JSON.

## Purpose

Generate the release notes of a version from the archived changes, so the
changelog and the release body no longer have to be written by hand.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: `codev changelog` selects the changes archived between two git refs

`codev changelog [--since <ref>] [--until <ref>]` SHALL include exactly the
changes whose folder is present under `_codev/changes/archive/` at `--until`
and absent from it at `--since`. Without `--until`, the working tree MUST be
used, archived changes not yet committed included. Without `--since`, the
most recent tag reachable from `--until` MUST be used, and when no tag is
reachable, every archived change at `--until` MUST be included.

#### Scenario: Changes archived between two tags

- **GIVEN** a repository where `v0.1.0` has the archived changes `a` and `b`
- **AND** `v0.2.0` has the archived changes `a`, `b`, `c` and `d`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --since v0.1.0 --until v0.2.0`
- **THEN** the output holds the release notes of `c` and `d` only

#### Scenario: Default range since the last tag

- **GIVEN** a repository whose last tag `v0.2.0` has the archived change `c`
- **AND** a change `e` archived in the working tree after that tag, not
  committed
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog`
- **THEN** the output holds the release note of `e` and not that of `c`

#### Scenario: No tag at all

- **GIVEN** a repository without any tag and with two archived changes
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog`
- **THEN** the output holds the release notes of both changes

#### Scenario: Unknown ref

- **GIVEN** a repository without a ref named `v9.9.9`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --since v9.9.9`
- **THEN** the command fails with the stable code `unknown_ref` naming
  `v9.9.9`
- **AND** nothing is printed on stdout except, with `--json`, the error
  document

#### Scenario: A ref that looks like an option is not an option

- **GIVEN** any repository
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --since=--output=/tmp/x`
- **THEN** the command fails with `unknown_ref`
- **AND** no file is created or modified

#### Scenario: Outside a git repository

- **GIVEN** a codev project that is not in a git repository
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --since v0.1.0`
- **THEN** the command fails with the stable code `not_a_git_repository`

### Requirement: Release notes are grouped by category, breaking items first

The output SHALL group the release-note items of the selected changes under
one section per category, in the order `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`,
`Removed`, `Fixed`, `Security`, omitting empty categories. Within a
category, items starting with `**BREAKING**` MUST come first, then the
others; within each of these two groups, items MUST follow the archive
order of their change (archive date, then change name), then their order in
the proposal. A change whose release note is `None` MUST contribute no item.

#### Scenario: Grouping and order

- **GIVEN** a change `2026-10-01-x` with `- Fixed: Fix one.` and
  `- Added: Add one.`
- **AND** a change `2026-10-02-y` with `- Added: **BREAKING** Add two.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog` over a range holding both
- **THEN** the output lists `### Added` with "**BREAKING** Add two." then
  "Add one.", followed by `### Fixed` with "Fix one."
- **AND** there is no `### Changed` section

#### Scenario: A `None` release note contributes nothing

- **GIVEN** a range whose only archived change has the release note `None`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog`
- **THEN** the output holds the heading and no category section
- **AND** the human output says that no change in the range has a release
  note

### Requirement: An archived change without a release note falls back on What Changes

When an archived change in the range has no `## Release note` section in
its proposal, `codev changelog` SHALL list each bullet of its
`## What Changes` section under `Changed`, and MUST report a warning
`release_note_missing` naming the change. A change with neither section
MUST contribute no item and MUST be reported by the same warning. Warnings
MUST go to stderr in the human output and never into the generated notes.

#### Scenario: Change archived before release notes existed

- **GIVEN** an archived change `old` whose proposal has two What Changes
  bullets and no `## Release note`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog` over a range holding `old`
- **THEN** both bullets appear under `### Changed`
- **AND** stderr carries a `release_note_missing` warning naming `old`

#### Scenario: Malformed release note in an archived change

- **GIVEN** an archived change whose release note holds the bullet
  `- Improved: Faster.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog` over a range holding it
- **THEN** the bullet is left out of the notes
- **AND** a warning `release_note_invalid_category` names the change and
  the line

### Requirement: Output formats of `codev changelog`

By default `codev changelog` SHALL print Markdown in the Keep a Changelog
form: a version heading, then one `### <Category>` section per category
with one `- <text>` bullet per item. The heading MUST be
`## [<version>] - <YYYY-MM-DD>` when `--until` is a tag, `<version>` being
the tag without a leading `v` and the date that of the tagged commit, and
`## [Unreleased]` otherwise. `--no-heading` MUST omit the version heading
and keep the rest. `--json` MUST write exactly one JSON document to stdout:
the resolved `since` and `until`, the list of included changes, the items
by category each with its text, `breaking` flag and source change, the
warnings, and a root `status` array where execution errors land.

#### Scenario: Heading of a tagged release

- **GIVEN** a tag `v0.3.0` on a commit dated 2026-10-20
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --until v0.3.0`
- **THEN** the first line of the output is `## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-20`

#### Scenario: Unreleased heading and body only

- **GIVEN** a repository with changes archived since its last tag
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog`
- **THEN** the first line of the output is `## [Unreleased]`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --no-heading`
- **THEN** the output starts with a `### <Category>` line

#### Scenario: JSON output

- **GIVEN** a range holding one change with one `Added` item
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --json`
- **THEN** stdout carries a single JSON document with that change, that
  item marked `"breaking": false`, and an empty `status`

#### Scenario: JSON output on an error

- **GIVEN** a repository without a ref named `nope`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog --since nope --json`
- **THEN** stdout carries a single JSON document with empty lists and a
  `status` entry with the code `unknown_ref`
- **AND** the exit code is non-zero

### Requirement: The `changelog` command is read-only

`codev changelog` MUST NOT write, move or delete any file, nor create,
move or delete any git ref, whatever its options.

#### Scenario: Generating notes leaves the repository untouched

- **GIVEN** a repository with a clean working tree and a `CHANGELOG.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev changelog`
- **THEN** the working tree is still clean and `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: The default schema gives each artifact a role with "Done when" criteria

The instruction of each artifact of the embedded `spec-driven` schema, as
returned by `codev instructions <artifact> --json`, SHALL start with a role
block: a `Role:` line naming the role and what it owns, followed by a
`Done when:` list of checkable criteria. The roles are:

- `proposal` — product owner, owns why and what;
- `specs` — QA analyst, owns observable behavior;
- `design` — architect, owns how;
- `tasks` — tech lead, owns sequencing and verification.

The tech lead's criteria MUST require that the documentation affected by
the change is updated in a task, or that the plan states none is affected;
that every spec scenario is covered by an automated test written in a task,
a manual check being acceptable only when automation is impossible and with
the reason stated; and that tests follow the project's existing test suite,
the testing conventions of its language, and its `rules`. The `proposal`
instruction MUST ask the Impact section to name the affected documentation.

The `proposal` instruction MUST also ask for a `## Release note` section
written for end users — bullets `- <Category>: <text>` with Category among
`Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`, `Security`, a breaking
item starting with `**BREAKING**`, or the single line `None` for a change
users will not notice — and the product owner's `Done when:` list MUST
include it. The `proposal` template returned with it MUST contain that
section, after Impact.

The rest of each instruction MUST stay as before. A custom schema's
instructions MUST be returned as written, without any role block added by
codev.

#### Scenario: The proposal instruction starts with the product owner role

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions proposal --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` starts with `Role: product owner`
- **AND** it contains a `Done when:` list that includes marking every
  breaking change with **BREAKING**
- **AND** it asks the Impact section to name the affected documentation

#### Scenario: The proposal instruction asks for a categorized release note

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions proposal --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** its `Done when:` list includes a release note written for end
  users, categorized, with breaking items marked, or `None`
- **AND** `instruction` names the six accepted categories
- **AND** `template` contains a `## Release note` heading after
  `## Impact`

#### Scenario: The tasks criteria cover every spec scenario

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions tasks --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` starts with `Role: tech lead`
- **AND** its `Done when:` list requires every spec scenario to be covered
  by at least one task's verification

#### Scenario: The tasks criteria require documentation and automated tests

- **GIVEN** a change using the `spec-driven` schema
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions tasks --change <name> --json`
- **THEN** its `Done when:` list requires the affected documentation to be
  updated in a task, or the plan to state that none is affected
- **AND** it requires every spec scenario to be covered by an automated
  test, a manual check only when automation is impossible, with the reason
- **AND** it requires tests to follow the project's existing test suite,
  the conventions of its language and its `rules`

#### Scenario: A custom schema gets no role block

- **GIVEN** a change using a project schema whose artifact instruction has
  no role block
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev instructions <artifact> --change <name>
  --json`
- **THEN** `instruction` is the schema's text, with no `Role:` line added
- **AND** no `## Release note` section is added to its template

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The release note of a change's proposal is checked

When an active change has a `proposal.md`, validation SHALL check its
`## Release note` section. The section MUST hold either the single line
`None`, or one or more bullets of the form `- <Category>: <text>`, where
`<Category>` is one of `Added`, `Changed`, `Deprecated`, `Removed`, `Fixed`,
`Security` (exact case) and `<text>` is not empty; a bullet's text MAY
continue on indented lines, and HTML comments are ignored. Validation MUST
report, with the line concerned:

- an error `release_note_invalid_category` for an unknown category;
- an error `release_note_malformed` for a line that is neither a bullet of
  that form, its continuation, nor `None`;
- an error `release_note_empty` for a section with no item and no `None`,
  or a bullet with no text;
- an error `release_note_none_with_items` when `None` sits next to items;
- a warning `release_note_missing` when the proposal has no
  `## Release note` section.

A change without `proposal.md` MUST get no release-note finding. Archived
changes are not validated and MUST NOT be affected.

#### Scenario: Well-formed release note

- **GIVEN** a change whose proposal has `## Release note` with
  `- Added: A new command.` and `- Changed: **BREAKING** A renamed flag.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no release-note finding is reported

#### Scenario: `None` is accepted

- **GIVEN** a change whose release note is the single line `None`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no release-note finding is reported

#### Scenario: Unknown category

- **GIVEN** a change whose release note holds `- Improved: Faster startup.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** an error `release_note_invalid_category` reports that line and
  lists the accepted categories
- **AND** the exit code is non-zero

#### Scenario: Bullet without a category

- **GIVEN** a change whose release note holds `- Faster startup.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** an error `release_note_malformed` reports that line

#### Scenario: Empty section

- **GIVEN** a change whose `## Release note` section holds only the
  template's HTML comment
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** an error `release_note_empty` reports the section heading

#### Scenario: `None` next to items

- **GIVEN** a change whose release note holds `None` and
  `- Fixed: A crash.`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** an error `release_note_none_with_items` is reported

#### Scenario: Proposal written before release notes

- **GIVEN** an active change whose proposal has no `## Release note`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** a warning `release_note_missing` is reported and the exit code
  is `0`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change> --strict`
- **THEN** the exit code is non-zero

#### Scenario: No proposal yet

- **GIVEN** a change just created, without `proposal.md`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate <change>`
- **THEN** no release-note finding is reported
